title: A journey, not a destination
header_line: My analysis of one book on habits. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Is your dream a journey or a destination?

A student said: I would change my mindset and see it as a work in progress, never really complete until the day you die. It is okay to have revisions, and there is no risk in making an effort, ripping the page in half and starting over.
I said: that is the trick, make it a journey, not a destination.

I said that in a film I love, a man is addicted to adopting new identities as the journey. I asked: why not cheat and believe I am already that successful writer? If I believe it, any act I do will never be as powerful as the consciousness that accompanies the act.
A student said: it is like giving yourself the reward before doing the work. Another said: it is speaking it into existence. It is the essence that gives it power, and then you have to embody it.

A student said: build it like a character, with traits, personality, behaviors. Say: this is the person I am striving to become. Add more and more of that character's behaviors to your day until it becomes the fabric of your reality.
I said: you visualize the intention, and then you become the visualization. I really think you become the character.
What would a person who has already done this do in the next hour?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write a goal you treat as a destination.
Write how it could be a work in progress.
Write the character you want to become and three behaviors.
Write one behavior you will do today as that person.
Write what you will do if the page needs to be ripped and redone.

check.q: What did I say to make it?
What did a student say about building a character?
choices: Give it traits and behaviors and add them to your day

check.q: What did a student say it is like?
choices: Giving yourself the reward before the work

recap: Make it a work in progress. Act as the person you are becoming.
